\paragraph{Extended validation ($n{=}32$).}
Adding Cheetah Run configurations ($n{=}9$) to the Walker analysis increases the evaluation set to $n{=}32$ ($n_{\text{pos}}{=}11$, $n_{\text{neg}}{=}21$). At the $1.5\times$ threshold, AUROC rises to $0.961$ with TPR${=}1.00$, FPR${=}0.143$ (3/21), and F1${=}0.880$. The three false positives are identical to the Walker-only analysis: exp\_047 ($1.71\times$, frozen transient), exp\_057 ($1.88\times$, frozen transient), and 008e\_v3 seed~2 ($3.78\times$, IRD). The Cheetah subset achieves perfect separation (AUROC${=}1.000$, 3/3 true positives, 0/6 false positives at $1.5\times$), suggesting that CIVO's higher severity in Cheetah (NVE up to $108\times$) widens the decision boundary.

\paragraph{Comprehensive validation ($n{=}56$).}
Expanding the evaluation set to all classifiable experiments yields $n{=}56$ ($n_{\text{pos}}{=}24$, $n_{\text{neg}}{=}32$), spanning Walker Walk, Cheetah Run, and multiple intervention configurations (SGS, TCN, dual-critic, frozen embedding). At the $1.5\times$ threshold: AUROC${=}0.990$, precision${=}0.889$, recall${=}1.000$, F1${=}0.941$, accuracy${=}53/56$. The three false positives are: exp\_008e\_v3\_subsample ($1.93\times$, mitigation config with transient VE spike), exp\_047 ($1.71\times$, frozen embedding transient), and exp\_057 ($1.88\times$, frozen embedding transient). All 24 CIVO-positive configurations are correctly detected (FN${=}0$), with CIVO-positive NVE ranging from $1.53\times$ (008d seed~3, late-onset) to $70.64\times$ (010b seed~0, Cheetah). The substantial increase in sample size from $n{=}32$ to $n{=}56$ strengthens confidence in the $1.5\times$ threshold as a robust diagnostic boundary.
